findings.title: Webhook signature in test_github_user_mismatch won't match the modified payload
findings.body: The test mutates webhook_event["installation"]["id"] and webhook_event["sender"]["login"] and then re-serializes with json.dumps(webhook_event), but it sends the hard-coded signature sha1=d184e6717f8bfbcc291ebc8c0756ee446c6c9486. That signature was computed over the original bytes of INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE; modifying any field changes the HMAC input, so the GitHub webhook endpoint will reject the request with a non-2xx response. The test will fail at `assert resp.status_code == 204`, the Integration record is never created, and the subsequent user-mismatch branch in GitHubInstallation is therefore never exercised. The new security check is added without a working test that proves it actually rejects a mismatched sender.

findings.title: KeyError/TypeError if integration metadata has no 'sender'
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch() compares pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. The webhook handler only writes the sender key when the webhook payload provides one, and build_integration only copies it when state.get("sender") is truthy, so pre-existing integrations (and any future flow where the webhook does not include a sender) can have no "sender" key, or a None value. Subscripting None or accessing a missing key raises TypeError/KeyError, which surfaces as an unhandled 500 to the user instead of the intended "Invalid installation request." page. The access should use a safe lookup such as integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login") and treat a missing sender as a mismatch (or a separate error).

findings.title: safe_urlopen to GitHub token endpoint is outside the try/except
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch(), safe_urlread and parse_qsl are wrapped in `try/except Exception` so any decode/parse failure yields an empty payload and triggers the error page. The preceding `req = safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` call is NOT inside that try block, so any network error, DNS failure, timeout, or non-2xx from safe_urlopen propagates out of dispatch and crashes the request as a 500 instead of returning the error page. The same problem applies to the immediately following `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` call at line 434, which is also outside the try block. Both should be wrapped so all token-exchange failures produce the same user-visible error response.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 branch
findings.body: The test name and the responses.replace(...status=404) suggest it is verifying the path where get_installation_info returns 404 (which should produce "The GitHub installation could not be found."). In the new flow, the first GET (with only installation_id) hits OAuthLoginView, which binds the id and redirects to GitHub OAuth without ever calling get_installation_info. The second GET uses state='ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05' which cannot equal pipeline.signature, so the response is the generic state-mismatch error page ("Invalid installation request.") rather than the installation-not-found error. The build_integration 404 branch is therefore no longer covered by any test, and the renamed assertion no longer checks what the test name implies.

findings.title: No audit log when authenticated GitHub user does not match installation sender
findings.body: The new check that rejects an installation when the OAuth-authenticated GitHub login differs from integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] is exactly the attack scenario this PR is designed to catch (a Sentry user trying to claim a GitHub app installation that was installed by a different GitHub identity). The branch only renders an error page and silently drops the request. A warning/error log entry containing the Sentry org, the installation_id, the authenticated login, and the recorded sender should be emitted so security teams can detect and investigate these attempts.
